# Articulated Demo Room MuJoCo Joint Rebuild

## Goal

Rebuild the original viewer articulation layer inside MuJoCo.

The source viewer scene contains:

```text
3 articulated objects
8 joints
```

This note records the first MuJoCo version where those joints exist as MJCF joints.

## Generated File

```text
/home/users/dazhi.sun-labs/projects/week5_note/pipeline/articulated_demo_mujoco/xml/articulated_demo_with_joints.xml
```

## MuJoCo Load Result

```text
nbody = 10
ngeom = 86
nmesh = 85
njnt = 8
nq = 8
```

Joint names:

```text
frame_to_door
left_hinge
right_hinge
body_to_front_door
body_to_sliding_tray
tray_to_turntable
body_to_upper_knob
body_to_lower_knob
```

## Render Outputs

```text
outputs/articulated_joints_closed_top.png
outputs/articulated_joints_closed_diag.png
outputs/articulated_joints_open_top.png
outputs/articulated_joints_open_diag.png
outputs/articulated_joints_motion.gif
outputs/joint_render_summary.json
```

## What Works

- MuJoCo loads the complex scene with 8 joints.
- The joint names match the original viewer/Articraft articulation names.
- Closed and open poses can be rendered by setting `data.qpos`.
- A motion GIF can be generated by interpolating joint positions.

## Current Limitation

This is a kinematic joint visualization, not a full robot-control task.

The demo directly sets joint positions in `data.qpos`. It does not yet:

- use actuators to control the joints dynamically;
- add a robot;
- simulate contact-rich manipulation;
- validate successful robot interaction.

## Next Step

Add simple actuators for selected joints, then test one small task first:

```text
open entry door
```

After that, add a mobile robot or manipulator in a separate test.
